prompt: An 8 GB VM is live-migrated with pre-copy over a link moving 1 GB/s, while the guest dirties 250 MB/s. Assuming every dirtied page is distinct, how much data is copied in round 3?

options.explanation: That is the amount dirtied during round 1, which is what round 2 copies.
Correct. Round 1 copies 8 GB in 8 s (2 GB dirtied); round 2 copies 2 GB in 2 s (500 MB dirtied); round 3 copies those 500 MB.
That is what is dirtied *during* round 3, which round 4 would copy.
Only round 1 copies all of memory; later rounds copy just pages dirtied since the previous round.

workedExample:
Using decimal units and constant effective rates, each round copies what the guest dirtied during the previous round:

```formula
r = d / b = (0.25 GB/s) / (1 GB/s)
r = 0.25
D_1 = 8 GB
t_1 = 8 GB / (1 GB/s) = 8 s
D_2 = d t_1 = 0.25 GB/s × 8 s = 2 GB
D_3 = r D_2 = 0.25 × 2 GB
D_3 = 0.5 GB = 500 MB
where
r: the shrink ratio, dirtying rate divided by copy rate (no unit)
d: the rate the guest dirties distinct pages, 250 MB/s = 0.25 GB/s
b: the effective copy rate, 1 GB/s
D_1, D_2, D_3: the data copied in rounds 1, 2 and 3
t_1: the time round 1 takes, in seconds (s)
GB: gigabyte, 1000 MB in decimal units
MB: megabyte
GB/s: gigabytes per second
s: seconds
In words: each round is a quarter the size of the one before, so round 3 copies 500 MB.
```

Later memory-transfer sets shrink in this toy model; total downtime also includes CPU/device and switchover work.

prompt: In the constant-rate pre-copy model, distinct dirty-page production remains 1.5 GB/s while effective copying is 1.25 GB/s, and the dirty working set stays large. What follows?

options.text: It finishes after more rounds than usual
options.explanation: More rounds alone do not shrink the set in this model. Real dirty sets are bounded by guest memory and may change over time.

options.text: The dirty set does not shrink under this model; live migration needs a changed policy, lower dirtying, more bandwidth or a longer stop phase
options.explanation: Correct. The model has ratio 1.2, so copying cannot reduce the dirty set while these assumptions persist.

options.text: It completes in one round because the database is in memory
options.explanation: Being in memory is exactly the problem: all that memory is changing fast.

options.text: The destination host copies pages back to the source
options.explanation: Pages only flow source to destination in pre-copy.

workedExample:
Compute the shrink ratio of the model:

```formula
r = d / b
r = (1.5 GB/s) / (1.25 GB/s) = 1.2
where
r: the shrink ratio: each round's data as a fraction of the previous round's (no unit)
d: the rate the guest dirties distinct pages, in gigabytes per second (GB/s)
b: the effective copy rate, in GB/s
GB/s: gigabytes per second
In words: the guest dirties 1.2 times as much data as can be copied in the same time, so each round leaves at least as much to copy as the last.
```

Under a sustained large dirty working set, ordinary pre-copy does not reduce remaining data. Throttling may reduce dirtying; more copy bandwidth may help; post-copy changes the failure/performance tradeoff; stop-and-copy accepts more pause time. Raw repeated writes to the same page would not justify this model.
